hookClip: India will always have a boss. Spain will always have lunch. Here's what to do — and what not to — in India and Spain.
countryADosClip: India. Address your manager as Sir, Ma'am, or Boss — well past your first year. Route requests up the chain and wait for sign-off, even on small matters.
countryADosScene: A modern open-plan office floor in Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex business district, glass towers visible through floor-to-ceiling windows behind her, Priya standing in the aisle between desks, weight shifted slightly to one hip, hands loosely clasped in front of her, face and eyes directly toward camera.
countryADosOutfit: A structured deep teal kurta over tailored cream trousers, block-heeled tan sandals
countryADontsClip: India. Don't switch to first names with a skip-level manager uninvited. Don't email the CEO directly to save everyone time. Don't assume silence or ambiguous body language means agreement.
countryADontsScene: A glass-walled meeting room in a modern Mumbai office tower, a long conference table behind her and city buildings visible through the window, Priya standing facing the camera with her weight on her right leg, arms relaxed at her sides.
countryADontsOutfit: A fitted burgundy kurta-style top with a mandarin collar over slim charcoal trousers and tan leather loafers.
countryBDosClip: Spain. Use usted with senior colleagues until they invite tú. Build rapport over a long lunch before asking for a favour. Push back on an unreasonable deadline — it reads as competent, not insubordinate.
countryBDosScene: A sunlit terrace restaurant in Madrid's business district, the Gran Vía visible in the background, Priya standing at the edge of the terrace facing the camera with her weight on her left leg, hands resting loosely at her sides.
countryBDosOutfit: A lightweight cream linen blazer over a dusty rose blouse, wide-leg camel trousers and white leather sandals.
countryBDosCaptions: Build rapport over a long lunch
countryBDontsClip: Spain. Don't assume first names from day one mean the hierarchy is gone. Don't expect a major decision to be settled by email alone. Don't schedule anything urgent for August and expect it to move.
countryBDontsScene: A co-working space in Barcelona's 22@ innovation district, floor-to-ceiling windows with the district's low skyline behind her, Priya standing facing the camera with a slight angle to her body, hands clasped loosely in front of her.
countryBDontsOutfit: A sleeveless structured navy dress with a modest neckline and a thin gold belt, paired with tan block-heel mules.
